ACTUAL ISSUE: the Sabbath insertions keep their printed parentheses as literal text, and none of the conditionals has @type. This affects 6 conditionals in Hebrew (segments 2, 4, 6, 10, 12, 16) and 6 in English (2, 4, 6, 10, 12, 14). JLPTEI-3 §'How an undecided scope is set off' and the ODD definition of j:conditional/@type say that when the source itself marks a passage off with parentheses, the conditional takes type="marked" and the exporter reproduces the standard delimiters. The current encoding causes three problems: (a) when Shabbat is true, literal parentheses are printed inside the running prayer text; (b) when undecided, the two Melokh scopes have an instruction note and no @type, so the processor adds a closing delimiter of its own after the literal ')'; (c) the source prints '(אם שבת. …)' with the label inside the parenthesis, but the encoding puts the label before the '(' and the parenthesis around the prayer words only. Using type="marked" with the parentheses taken out of the text fixes all three, and keeps the Rashi labels where they belong, as the conditional's own instruction notes.

PASS: the two 'אם שבת.' labels are tei:note type="instruction" xml:lang="he" placed as the j:conditional's single note before j:all, which fits the ODD content model and counts as a condition rubric under 'Kinds of rubric'. They have no rend and no font styling. The vattitten insertions and the seal have no label in the print and get no invented note. Every Sabbath clause stays inside its original paragraph.

DELIBERATE ARCHITECTURE: (מלכנו) has no stated condition, so it stays literal text, outside any choice or conditional. Under the guidelines it is a textual variant (opensiddur:variant with a condition URN), but adding one would invent an inclusion setting and a registry identity. Leaving it literal matches the instruction. The only consequence is that it is always output.

MINOR, recommended: JLPTEI-3 says that when a seg[@source] quotation also needs a correspondence, its milestone goes before the semantic span. All six quotations instead put the chapter and verse milestones inside the seg, with bare terminators at its end. The resolved extents are identical, so nothing changes in scope. Either move the milestones outside the seg or document this form.

OBSERVATION: the context milestone 'milestone unit="chapter" n="…"' has no corresp, so under URN-scope rule 3 it is formally a chapter terminator that opens nothing. It is harmless, because it comes before the verse milestone and no chapter scope is open in these files. It claims no whole-chapter URN, which matches the intent.
